messages:
nico-devex: A customer hit a weird combo bug when upgrading to @redwood/sdk@5.0.0: their Worker bundle fails at runtime with an obscure sourcemap/exports error after bundling with esbuild. Error: `Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` pointing into a generated sourcemap loader.

micah-eng: Can you paste the package.json exports and the import line? Curious if the bundler inlines the wrong file due to a nested subpath.

nico-devex: Import in sample: `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'`. package.json exports: 

nico-devex: ```json
nico-devex: "exports": { "./package.json": "./package.json", ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", "default": "./dist/index.cjs" }, "./internal/*": "./dist/internal/*.js" }
nico-devex: ```

tara-runtime: Hmm, we added a weird `default` conditional earlier to try to preserve CJS default interop. Edge loaders ignore nonstandard keys, so some bundlers fall back to the wildcard `./internal/*` and end up pulling internal runtime helpers that expect a different initialization path. That can cause recursion if the internal entry re-exports the index which points back into internal.

sam-qa: Repro steps I ran: clone onboarding-sample + `npm i @redwood/sdk@5.0.0` + `esbuild --bundle index.js --platform=browser --outfile=out.js` then `wrangler dev`. Repro: stack overflow in the generated bundle referencing `__export_star` helpers; sourcemap points to a tiny helper in dist/internal/loader.js.

micah-eng: Two separate but related issues here: 1) exports map allowed internal wildcard that leaked private files; 2) our ESM build removed the default export so default-import users trigger the fallback path in some bundlers that try require -> cjs path -> internal shim.

nico-devex: TypeScript also reported missing types in their monorepo build: "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'" even though we ship index.d.ts in dist. Some TS setups don't follow conditional types in exports and won't pick up dist/index.d.ts unless we expose a top-level "types" field.

tara-runtime: Short-term fix: revert the `./internal/*` wildcard and remove the nonstandard `default` key from exports. Add top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" and include an explicit ESM default shim: in dist/index.mjs do `export { createClient as default } from './client.js'`. That should stop bundlers from attempting deep-internal resolution.

sam-qa: I'll add CI smoke tests that bundle the published tgz with esbuild (browser + node), Bun, and a Workers dev run. Also add a tsc check that installs the package and runs `tsc --noEmit` against sample code to ensure types resolve.

micah-eng: For longer-term: update the publishing pipeline to validate export map semantics with a small script that checks for unintended wildcards and ensures every export target is present and not under dist/internal unless explicitly public. Also we should enumerate supported import shapes in CHANGELOG.

pkg-bot: npm-publish: queued 5.0.1 patch (revert wildcard, add top-level types, add ESM default shim). Release draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1102

nico-devex: I'm going to push a small sample diff to onboarding-samples updating imports to named import `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` and add a note to migration guide about ESM/CJS differences. Will update the customer once 5.0.1 is published. :thumbsup:
